title.narrative: Buenos Aires – Mitre Passenger Railway Line Modernization Project

description.narrative: The Project Development Objectives (PDO) of the Argentina Buenos Aires – Mitre Passenger Railway Line Modernization Project are to: (a) improve the reliability and safety of the Mitre Line; and (b) increase accessibility in the Metropolitan Area of Buenos Aires. The proposed project has three components, all three components contribute to climate mitigation and incorporate climate adaptation measures to enhance the resilience of the railway system in Buenos Aires Metropolitan Area. Component 1: Retiro railyard upgrade, extension and renewal; Component 2: Mitre Line upgrade; and Component 3: Institutional strengthening and project management.
The Project Development Objectives are to: (a) improve the reliability and safety of the Mitre Line; and (b) increase accessibility in the Metropolitan Area of Buenos Aires.

condition.narrative: Section 3.01 of the Loan Agreement. The Borrower, through MTR, shall carry out the Project and cause ADIFSE to carry out ADIFSE'sRespective Parts of the Project, all in accordance with the provisions of Article V of the General Conditions and Schedule 2 tothisAgreement.
Section I. of Schedule 2 to the Loan Agreement. The Borrower shall carry out the Project in accordance with the ImplementationArrangements set out in Section I, Schedule 2 to the Loan Agreement.

Section I.A.1 of Schedule 2 to the Loan Agreement. The Borrower, through the MTR, shall operate and maintain at all times duringProject implementation, the DGPPSE, with structure, functions, and responsibilities acceptable to the Bank, as set forth in theOperational Manual.

Section I.A.2 of Schedule 2 to the Loan Agreement. The Borrower, through the MTR, shall ensure that the DGPPSE is at all timesduring Project implementation adequately staffed with professionals necessary to fulfill its functions.

Section I.B of Schedule 2 to the Loan Agreement. The Borrower, through MTR, shall make part of the proceeds of the Loan availableto ADIFSE on a non-reimbursable basis, under a transfer, assistance, and execution agreement between the Borrower, through MTR andADIFSE, under terms and conditions approved by the Bank.

title.narrative: Inferred beneficiaries of improved access to sustainable transport infrastructure and services
Passengers per day in the Mitre Line

comment.narrative: Passenger usage dropped significantly. Daily ridership fell from 131,600 in June 2024 to 101,900 in June 2025. This reduction is attributed to a long-term change in mobility patterns, lower fare control staffing, increased work windows, and possibly underreporting of informal fare evasion.

Number of railway incidents and accidents per million train-km linked to safety issues on the Mitre Line

comment.narrative: Safety performance improved across the Mitre Line, with the number of railway incidents and accidents per million train kilometers falling from 11 to 8. This positive trend is particularly evident in branches where infrastructure improvements are nearing completion (Retiro station). However, incident concentration remains higher on diesel branches like Zárate and Capilla del Señor. The ongoing works are expected to further support the achievement of this indicator.

title.narrative: Share of Mitre Line users satisfied with overall railway service, differentiated by gender

comment.narrative: Passenger satisfaction declined from 70.8% to 63.1%, based on the share of users rating their experience as satisfactory. This drop follows a change in survey methodology implemented in January 2025, shifting from a 1–10 scale to a 1–5 scale.

title.narrative: Share of trains operating on the Mitre Line with less than a five-minute delay vs. the scheduled timeline

comment.narrative: Reliability performance on the Mitre Line has remained broadly stable but continues to fluctuate across branches due to ongoing infrastructure constraints and temporary operational disruptions associated with construction works. The Suárez and Mitre branches are still affected by recurrent signaling failures, cable theft incidents, and power supply issues. The Retiro–Tigre branch continues to perform comparatively better, although improvements remain linked to timetable optimization rather than underlying infrastructure conditions. As the renewal of track, signaling, and electrification systems advances, particularly the Maldonado–Tigre corridor works and the Retiro yard commissioning expected for early 2026, reliability is projected to improve sustainably.

title.narrative: Share of trains operating on the Mitre Line with less than a five-minute delay vs. the scheduled timeline

comment.narrative: From June 2024 to June 2025, reliability indicators (share of trains arriving with less than 5 minutes of delay) declined slightly overall on the Mitre Line—from 79.28% to 77.54%—with mixed performance across branches. Service regularity declined on the Retiro–Suárez and Retiro–Mitre branches, while the Retiro–Tigre branch showed improvement primarily due to the implementation of a new timetable, rather than actual operational enhancements. Operations on the Suárez and Mitre branches were further affected by cable theft and signaling issues. This indicator is expected to be achieved once the current works are completed.

title.narrative: Jobs accessible in AMBA in less than 60 minutes

comment.narrative: The indicator has not been updated during this reporting period because its calculation depends on the multimodal accessibility model for the Metropolitan Area of Buenos Aires, which is currently being revised as part of the ongoing restructuring. The underlying datasets required for this metric are being adjusted to reflect changes in the scope and timing of supply-efficiency measures. Once the restructuring is finalized and updated network data are available, the indicator will be recalculated to ensure methodological consistency and accuracy.
